overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the posting time from its January 30 notice; no violation found on undisclosed topics or limits on public comment. Board ordered to comply in future.

allegations.summary: Notice for the January 30 meeting lacked the date and time of posting; the notice showed a posting date but no posting time.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to include the time that the January 30 notice was posted.

allegations.summary: Board discussed topics not listed on the January 30 notice: the chair's opening statement and the Department Head Reports, which lacked specific topics.
allegations.key_passage: Where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Chair or CAO limited a member of the public's speaking time at the January 30 meeting and told him to be silent.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law therefore gives discretion to the chair of a public body to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting, and to set limits on public participation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
